stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below -5.1%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $11.56 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-19, 30 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-18.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-29) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

The Series and DataFrame objects in pandas are powerful tools for exploring and analyzing data. Part of their power comes from a multifaceted approach to combining separate datasets. With pandas, you can merge, join, and concatenate your datasets, allowing you to unify and better understand your data as you analyze it.

In this tutorial, you’ll learn how and when to combine your data in pandas with:

stories.title: Top U.N. court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
stories.excerpt: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during the 2017 military operations in the northern Rakhine State.
stories.lead:
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya during its 2017 military operations in northern Rakhine State.

Delivering the judgment, Judge Yuji Iwasawa said the scale and nature of the military's actions went "well beyond what would be required to punish the population" and were instead "characteristic of an intent to destroy a substantial part of the group."

The judges estimated that around 815,000 Rohingya lived in northern Rakhine State before the operations, and concluded that around 10,000 were violently killed during the 2017 clearance campaign.

stories.title: Israeli military completes ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
stories.excerpt: Hamas condemned the incursion, which the Israeli military said was to dismantle a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.
stories.lead:
Israeli forces have completed a rare ground operation in part of central Gaza outside their control, the military says, a day after residents were ordered to evacuate.

Families fled their homes and tents on Wednesday as tanks advanced into an area east of Nuseirat refugee camp and onto the territory's main north-south road under the cover of artillery strikes.

The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel.

stories.lead:
ByKali HaysTechnology reporterSamira HussainNorth America business correspondent and Osmond ChiaBusiness reporter

Anthropic, the company behind AI chatbot Claude, has raised a record $81bn (£62bn) in a stock market debut that will make it one of the most valuable companies in the world.

A surge of investor appetite to buy shares in the loss-making business meant more stock was sold than originally planned. Anthropic's shares have been priced at $83, up from the proposed $70-$78 range.
